newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease in line with German bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease in line with German bunds.

text.p: Irish bonds eased across the board in late trade on Wednesday in line with bunds as the German market showed little enthusiasm to break out of its recent range before a national holiday on Thursday.

Several continental European markets are closed for the Ascension Day holiday on Thursday and dealers said many investors are expected to take advantage of the long weekend and stay away on Friday as well.
"It has been really quiet. Most of those in Germany seem to be gone home since lunchtime," one dealer said.
"Basically we are just keeping an eye on the currencies. We are not out of the woods there yet," the dealer added.

By 1520 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 30 pence from Tuesday's close at 101.55 to yield 6.08 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 18 pence from the close at 108.82 to yield 6.69 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 154 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 92 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area.
